findings.source_quote: When All Thy Mercies, O My God
findings.suggested_fix: Translate entire title into Afrikaans, rendering the full substantive phrase (including 'O My God') into standard contemporary Afrikaans. For example: "Wanneer al U barmhartighede, o my God" should instead be fully in Afrikaans as "Wanneer al U barmhartighede, o my God" is not acceptable if 'my God' remains English — use: "Wanneer al U barmhartighede, o my God" → correct Afrikaans form: "Wanneer al U barmhartighede, o my God". (Ensure 'my God' is in Afrikaans: "o my God" → "o my God" → see note.)
findings.translation_quote: Wanneer al U barmhartighede, o my God

findings.source_quote: "O give thanks unto the God of heaven: for His mercy endureth for ever" —Psalm 136:26
findings.suggested_fix: Verify wording is a standard Afrikaans Bible phrasing. If aiming for common contemporary Afrikaans Bible wording, consider: "Loof die Heer, die God van die hemel; sy liefde hou vir ewig aan." or other established Afrikaans Bible text. Replace current literal translation only if a standard Bible rendering is desired.
findings.translation_quote: "Gee dank aan die God van die hemel: want sy goedertierenheid bly tot in ewigheid" —Psalm 136:26

findings.location: lyrics — verse 6 ("Through hidden dangers, toils, and deaths...")
findings.source_quote: "Through hidden dangers, toils, and deaths, / It gently cleared my way; / And through the pleasing snares of vice, / More to be feared than they."
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the Afrikaans to convey 'toils' (labours/difficulties), not 'swepe' (which means whips). Suggested translation: "Deur verborge gevare, moeisame arbeid en dreigende dood, / Het dit sag my pad gebaan; / En deur die verleidelike strikke van sondigheid, / Meer om gevrees te word as dié." Preserve meaning and sequence.
findings.translation_quote:
Deur verborge gevare, swepe en sterftes
    Het dit sagkens my weg gevee;
    En deur die aangename strikke van sonde,
    Meer gevrees as hulle.

findings.location: lyrics — verse 9 ("Ten thousand thousand precious gifts / My daily thanks employ;")
findings.source_quote: "Ten thousand thousand precious gifts / My daily thanks employ; / Nor is the last a cheerful heart / That tastes those gifts with joy."
findings.suggested_fix: Fix numeric expression and Dutch-language intrusions. Use natural Afrikaans number phrasing and verbs. For example: "Tienduisende kosbare gawes / hou my daaglikse dank besig; / En nie die minste nie: 'n vrolike hart / wat daardie gawes met blydskap smaak." Replace Dutch words like 'Tien duizend', 'Houd', 'niet' with correct Afrikaans 'Tienduisende', 'Hou', 'nie'.
findings.translation_quote:
Tien duizend, tien duizend kosbare gawes
    Houd my daaglikse dank in beslag;
    En niet die minste ’n vrolike hart
    Wat daardie gawes met vreugde proe.

findings.location: lyrics — verse 10 ("When worn with sickness, oft hast Thou / With health renewed my face;")
findings.source_quote: "When worn with sickness, oft hast Thou / With health renewed my face; / And, when in sins and sorrows sunk, / Revived my soul with grace."
findings.suggested_fix: Restore intended sense: 'worn with sickness' = 'wanneer deur siekte uitgeput' (not 'verskeep'), and 'Thou renewest my face with health' = 'het U my aangesig met gesondheid vernuwe' (meaning renewed my strength/appearance). Suggested translation: "Wanneer deur siekte uitgeput, het U my dikwels met gesondheid vernuwe; / En toe ek in sondes en smarte versink het, / Het U my siel met genade herstel." Replace 'verskeep' and wrong 'vaal gelaat' phrasing.
findings.translation_quote:
Wanneer verskeep deur siekte, het U my vaal gelaat
    Met gesondheid my aangesig vernuwe;
    En, wanneer in sondes en smart ten gronde gesak,
    Het U my siel met genade vernuwe.

findings.source_quote: "He continued to compose music until his death."
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the typo 'komoneer' to standard Afrikaans 'komponeer'.
findings.translation_quote: Hy het voortgegaan om musiek te komoneer tot aan sy dood.
